title: AI boom likely stopped recession, top economist David Rosenberg says
excerpt: The AI boom is soaking up investor capital, shoring up economic growth, and showing signs of strain, David Rosenberg says.
content_html:
AI might be the one reason we're not in a recession, top economist David Rosenberg says

By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The AI boom is soaking up investor cash, staving off a recession, and showing signs of faltering, David Rosenberg says.

AI is "sapping the momentum out of the rest of business capital spending," the veteran economist said during the latest episode of the "Excess Returns" podcast.

Rosenberg estimated that 50% of all corporate investment is going toward AI-related items, and that segment of spending is growing around 18% annually in real terms, while capital spending in the "old economy" is declining.

He was responding to Richard Bernstein, the global head of macro at Janus Henderson Investors, saying that, similar to how the energy sector was "starved for capital" during the dot-com boom, money is flowing into building data centers instead of residential homes, fueling the housing shortage and affordability crisis.

Rosenberg, known for calling both the dot-com and housing crashes, said the economic backdrop is very different now than during the internet bubble.

The Rosenberg Research president, previously Merrill Lynch's chief North American economist, said that "nobody was talking about a K-shaped economy back then. The consumer was really strong across the board. You can't say that today."

"When you strip out the AI spend, the economy is actually very weak," Rosenberg said. He pointed to the housing sector contracting and weakness in auto sales and non-tech manufacturing.

"Without the AI boom, we probably would be in a recession," he added.

The US economy grew at an annualized 1.5% in the second quarter of this year, down from 2.1% in the first quarter. It unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July, upending the Wall Street consensus that it would gain 85,000 jobs.

Just like in the lead-up to the 2008 financial crisis, Rosenberg said he expects debt investors to spot warning signs before stock investors do.

"I think the credit market will lead the ultimate rolling over of this AI trade," he said, pointing to early red flags such as rising financing costs and spreads on credit default swaps (CDS), a form of insurance against loan defaults, widening "pretty dramatically."

大卫·罗森伯格表示，人工智能的繁荣正在吸纳投资者的资金，避免经济衰退，但同时也显示出衰退的迹象。

这位资深经济学家在最新一期的“超额回报”播客中表示，人工智能正在“削弱其他企业资本支出的动力”。

罗森伯格估计，所有企业投资的 50% 将流向人工智能相关项目，该部分支出每年实际增长 18% 左右，而“旧经济”的资本支出正在下降。

他是在回应骏利亨德森投资公司(Janus Henderson Investors)全球宏观主管理查德·伯恩斯坦(Richard Bernstein)的回应，他表示，与互联网泡沫时期能源行业“缺乏资金”类似，资金正在流入数据中心建设而不是住宅，加剧了住房短缺和负担能力危机。

罗森伯格因称互联网泡沫和房地产崩盘而闻名，他表示，现在的经济背景与互联网泡沫时期有很大不同。

这位罗森伯格研究公司总裁、前美林公司北美首席经济学家表示，“当时没有人谈论K型经济。 消费者的整体表现确实很强劲。 今天你不能这么说。”

“当你剔除人工智能支出时，经济实际上非常疲软，”罗森伯格说。 他指出房地产行业萎缩以及汽车销售和非技术制造业疲软。

“如果没有人工智能的繁荣，我们可能会陷入衰退，”他补充道。

今年第二季度美国经济年化增长率为1.5%，低于第一季度的2.1%。 7月份，该公司出人意料地失去了23,000个工作岗位，颠覆了华尔街关于它将增加85,000个工作岗位的共识。

就像 2008 年金融危机爆发前一样，罗森伯格表示，他预计债务投资者会先于股票投资者发现警告信号。

他表示：“我认为信贷市场将引领人工智能交易的最终滚动。”他指出了早期的危险信号，例如融资成本上升和信用违约掉期（CDS）利差“大幅扩大”，信用违约掉期是一种针对贷款违约的保险形式。
